subject: Add passphrase key derivation for exported connection files
body:
Add passphrase key derivation for exported connection files

An export has to open on a machine that has no DPAPI key for it, so its key can
only come from what the user types. That makes it the one place an attacker
holding the file can guess offline, and the only place worth a slow KDF.

Argon2id rather than PBKDF2: its cost is memory as well as time, denying a GPU
the parallelism that makes PBKDF2 cheap to attack at scale. Affordable only
because an export derives once for the whole file, unlike the per-secret scheme.
Defaults are 64 MiB / 3 iterations / parallelism 4.

An export is a re-encrypted copy: the DPAPI-wrapped internal key is never
involved, so handing out an export cannot weaken the file it came from. The salt
is fresh per export, so exporting the same connections twice with the same
passphrase still yields two files with different keys, and disclosing one
export's key cannot unlock another.

The derivation parameters are recorded in the file, so changing the defaults
later cannot strand an existing export; importing honours what the file says.

Tests cover the round-trip, wrong keys, the fresh-salt guarantee, importing a
file written with older parameters, and that derivation is not accidentally fast.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: Argon2id passphrase export keys is sound, but builds on vindict6-only ConnectionFileProtection scheme absent from our fork (verified via grep); would need full redesign atop our PBKDF2/MasterPasswordGate stack.
